question: AB and CD are two chords in a circle with centre O and AD is a diameter. AB and CD produced meet at a point P outside the circle. If ∠APD = 25° and ∠DAP = 39°, then the measure of ∠CBD is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In ΔAPD, ∠ADP = 180° − (25° + 39°) = 116°.

Since C, D, P are collinear (CD produced), ∠ADC = 180° − 116° = 64°.

In ΔACD, ∠CAD = 90° − 64° = 26° (as ∠ACD = 90° for diameter AD).

Angles subtended by the same arc CD are equal: ∠CBD = ∠CAD = 26°.

**∴ The correct answer is 26°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** AD is the diameter. AB and CD produced meet at P. ∠APD = 25°, ∠DAP = 39°.

**Formula:** Sum of angles in a triangle = 180° | Angle in a semicircle = 90° | Angles in the same segment are equal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5dafc90f3d8d15a629f5f07c76b237f116758fb5eef211842e40bbf64bc58b53.png] 

⇒ In ΔAPD, sum of angles = 180°

⇒ ∠DAP + ∠APD + ∠ADP = 180°

⇒ 39° + 25° + ∠ADP = 180°

⇒ ∠ADP = 180° − 64° = 116°

⇒ Since C-D-P is a straight line, ∠ADC + ∠ADP = 180°

⇒ ∠ADC = 180° − 116° = 64°

⇒ In ΔACD, ∠ACD = 90° (Angle in a semicircle)

⇒ ∠CAD = 180° − (∠ACD + ∠ADC) = 180° − (90° + 64°) = 26°

⇒ ∠CBD and ∠CAD are angles in the same segment (subtended by arc CD)

⇒ ∠CBD = ∠CAD = 26°

**∴ The correct answer is 26°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle in a Semicircle

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of a circle is always a right angle (90°).

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc at any point on the remaining part of the circle are equal (∠CBD = ∠CAD).

Cyclic Quadrilateral Properties

The sum of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°, and an exterior angle is equal to the interior opposite angle.</p
